basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et bitumine linies intrinsecus et extrinsecus, et facies sic eam. Bitumen est'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et bitumine linies intrinsecus et extrinsecus, et facies sic eam. Bitumen est ferventissimum et violentissimum gluten, cujus haec virtus est, ut ligna quae ex eo fuerint lita, nec vermibus exedi, nec solis ardore, vel ventorum flatibus, vel aquarum possint inundatione dissolvi; unde quid aliud mystice in bitumine quam constantia fidei accipitur? Bituminatur autem arca intrinsecus et extrinsecus, et sic universe perficitur, dum et cogitationes electorum et opera, ne ullis vincantur aut decipiantur vitiorum incursibus, fidei in omnibus virtute muniuntur.
